pipeline.detail: Unwrapped phase, coherence, connected components and mask are read from the NISAR GUNW fixture exactly as distributed.
Phase is converted to line-of-sight range change using the wavelength derived from the product's own centre-frequency metadata.
Every pixel is classed VALID, CAUTION or EXCLUDED by transparent rules. Excluded pixels are never interpolated.

Unwrapped phase is relative. For zones and ranking, each pixel is compared with a plane fitted to its surroundings in the same unwrapped region, so motion shared by the whole area does not count as a local anomaly. The map's surface-motion layer stays relative to the scene median.
Contiguous groups of quality-approved pixels above a screening threshold become deformation zones; tiny groups are rejected.
Zones are intersected with OpenStreetMap roads; radar evidence is summarised along each road corridor.
A weighted sum of six visible factors gives the inspection priority score. Weights are perturbed to test ranking stability.

sign_convention: Positive LOS range change = ground moved away from the satellite along the radar line of sight between the reference (earlier) and secondary (later) acquisition.
sign_convention_basis: The NISAR GUNW product specification does not state the sign convention in words. TriageSAR derives it from the ISCE3 processing software, which forms the interferogram as reference x conj(secondary) with the reference being the earlier acquisition. The inspection ranking uses only the magnitude of the motion, so it does not depend on the sign. The NASA/JPL displacement maps for this event use the opposite convention (positive = towards the satellite).

quality_states.meaning: Passes every rule. Used in analysis.
Usable but weaker evidence. Used in analysis and flagged.

quality_rules.rationale: Low coherence means the radar signal decorrelated between the two dates; the phase is noise. Screening value.
Moderate coherence: phase is usable but noisier. Screening value.
The product marks these pixels as not reliably unwrapped (NISAR ATBD).
The phase offset of a small isolated region relative to its neighbours is ambiguous. Screening value.

quality_rules.rule: product mask: fill, water, or invalid sub-swath
quality_rules.rationale: Flags shipped with the product itself (NISAR GUNW specification).

threshold_rule: Each pixel is first compared with a plane fitted to the usable pixels of the same unwrapped region within a 4 km window around it. A pixel is a zone candidate when the absolute difference is at least max(3 cm, 3 x 1.4826 x MAD of all such differences). Zones smaller than 0.5 km2 are rejected. The floor, the multiplier and the minimum area were fixed before any real data were inspected; the local reference replaced a scene-median reference after the first real run found that the earthquake's broad motion swamped it.
score_formula: Inspection priority score = 100 x sum(weight x factor), each factor between 0 and 1

score_components.name: displacement_magnitude
score_components.label: Observed LOS motion at the road

score_components.name: overlap_extent
score_components.label: Length of road inside the zone

sensitivity: Every weight is perturbed by up to ±20% (12 one-at-a-time runs and 200 seeded random draws). If the top item changes in more than 20% of runs the ranking is labelled UNSTABLE.
corrections: The GUNW product ships ionosphere, troposphere and solid-Earth-tide layers but does not remove them from the unwrapped phase, and neither does TriageSAR. Road corridors are 250 m either side of the road; roads within 1000 m of a zone are listed.
limitations: One interferogram gives motion along one viewing direction only; horizontal motion parallel to the satellite track is almost invisible.

Values are relative, never absolute. Zones measure motion that differs from the surrounding 4 km, so motion that is smooth over many kilometres (such as most of an earthquake's broad deformation field) is deliberately not reported as a zone, even when it is large.
No atmospheric (ionosphere, troposphere) or solid-Earth-tide correction is applied, so long-wavelength atmospheric signal can be mistaken for motion.
Phase-unwrapping errors can create or hide jumps of half a wavelength; isolated small unwrapped regions are flagged CAUTION for this reason.
Vegetated, steep, water-covered or rapidly changing terrain loses coherence and is excluded: it is unobserved, not safe.
Road geometry and names come from OpenStreetMap and may be incomplete or out of date.
The NISAR product used is a PROVISIONAL (partially validated) release.
All thresholds and weights are screening values chosen for a prototype; they have not been calibrated against field inspections.
not_claimed: TriageSAR does not detect structural damage.
TriageSAR does not predict casualties or losses.
NISAR observations are not treated as ground truth.
The inspection priority score is not a probability, an accuracy or a statistical confidence.
